summary: Janice Dean Willis specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees in philosophy from Cornell University and a Ph.D. from Columbia under Alex Wayman. She held posts as Professor at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and teacher at Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Jann Ronis works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor David F. Germano and teachers Jeffrey Hopkins and Khenpo Sönam Tenpa. He held an attested post at the University of Virginia in 2007.

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under the supervision of Alex Wayman and studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He became Assistant Professor at Uppsala in 1908, succeeding Johansson in 1927.
Jaroslav Průšek was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Prague and its Faculty of Arts from around 1924 to 1930. He later taught Karel Werner.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied under Peter Oldmeadow at the University of Sydney and Alexis Sanderson at the University of Oxford (D.Phil. 2013). He held posts at Oxford (attested 2011), SOAS (attested 2020), and Alberta (attested 2021).

Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and held the Theiline Pigott McCone Chair in Humanities at Seattle University from 2014 to 2016.

Jason Matthew McCombs works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a B.S. at the University of Michigan and a PhD in 2014 at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by Gregory Schopen, where he was attested as lecturer in 2014.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at UT Austin and earned a PhD at the University of Washington (2001) under Richard Salomon. Posts include Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2013–2021) and Ruhr University Bochum (2009–2010).

Jason Protass works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016). He held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware and Naropa University, before earning a PhD at the University of Virginia supervised by Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1959–1963). He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley (~1969–1973), Harvard (1970–1978; 1998 as Diebold Professor), and Cornell University (1981–1985 as full professor).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Melbourne, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and National University of Singapore.
Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna from circa 1934 to 1938.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar. He held a post as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned doctorates from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, and held positions at McMaster, Banaras Hindu University, University of Marburg (1991–2012), and University of Innsbruck (~2008–2013).

Jaś Elsner specializes in archaeology, art history, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, Harvard, and Courtauld, he has held posts at Courtauld (~1992–1999), Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and the University of Oxford (2014).
Jean Dantinne was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, and held research and associate posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian educated at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He held major posts at EPHE (1941–1978), Collège de France (1951–1978), the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977), and EFEO (1956–1977).
